entries.expect: allows multiple jobs within the same workflow

propositions.formalization: DESCRIPTIVE: without a concurrency key, forall runs and jobs r1 != r2 of the same workflow, repository or owner account, r1 and r2 may run at the same time, including identical instances of one workflow.

semantic_ast.object: multiple jobs, workflow runs and owner-wide workflow runs, including instances of one workflow, to run concurrently by default
semantic_ast.subject: GitHub Actions

entries.expect: only one run can be pending in a concurrency group

propositions.formalization: DESCRIPTIVE: when concurrency is limited, pending(group) <= 1 by default and a further pending run cancels the previous one; queuing is an opt-in that allows several waiting runs in order.

exceptions: queuing, an opt-in, lets several runs wait and execute in order
semantic_ast.object: a concurrency group to one pending run by default, replacing the earlier pending run
semantic_ast.subject: GitHub Actions

entries.expect: A concurrency group can be any string or expression

propositions.formalization: DEFINITION: a workflow-level group is any string or expression whose contexts are within {github, inputs, vars}.

semantic_ast.object: any string or expression using only the github, inputs and vars contexts
semantic_ast.subject: a workflow-level concurrency group

entries.expect: A concurrency group can be any string or expression

propositions.formalization: DEFINITION: a job-level group is any string or expression whose contexts are within {github, inputs, vars, needs, strategy, matrix}.

semantic_ast.object: any string or expression using only the github, inputs, vars, needs, strategy and matrix contexts
semantic_ast.subject: a job-level concurrency group

entries.expect: at most one running job or workflow in a concurrency group at any time

propositions.formalization: CONSTRAINT: forall group g, |running(g)| <= 1; a run queued while running(g) is non-empty (same repository) is pending; by default the earlier pending run is canceled and the new run takes its place.

consequences: the earlier pending run is canceled and the new queued run takes its place
semantic_ast.object: a concurrency group to one running job or workflow, holding a newly queued run as pending and replacing any earlier pending run by default
preconditions: another job or workflow in the same group in the repository is in progress
semantic_ast.subject: GitHub Actions

entries.expect: at most one running and one pending job in a concurrency group

propositions.formalization: CONSTRAINT: forall group g, |running(g)| <= 1 and |pending(g)| <= 1; a run queued while running(g) is non-empty (same repository) is pending and replaces any earlier pending run, which is canceled.
preserved_differences: Where actions-nga does not apply the text states one running and one pending explicitly; with the flag it states one running and one pending by default, so the two wordings agree on the default behaviour.

consequences: the earlier pending run is canceled and the new queued run takes its place
semantic_ast.object: a concurrency group to one running and one pending job or workflow, replacing the earlier pending run
preconditions: another job or workflow in the same group in the repository is in progress
semantic_ast.subject: GitHub Actions

ambiguities: Evaluation of the cancel-in-progress expression is not specified beyond its allowed contexts; the model takes an already evaluated boolean.
propositions.formalization: CAPABILITY: cancel-in-progress = true additionally cancels the running run of the group; cancel-in-progress may be an expression over the allowed contexts.

semantic_ast.object: the currently running job or workflow in the same concurrency group
qualifiers: cancel-in-progress may be a conditional expression using the allowed contexts
semantic_ast.subject: cancel-in-progress: true

ambiguities: The text is silent on queue where actions-nga does not apply; the model rejects the key there rather than assume it is accepted.
propositions.formalization: CAPABILITY: queue in {single, max}, optional, default single; it allows more than one pending run to wait.

semantic_ast.object: more than one pending job or workflow run to wait in a concurrency group
semantic_ast.subject: the queue property

propositions.formalization: DEFINITION: queue = single: |pending(g)| <= 1; a newly queued run cancels and replaces the pending one.

semantic_ast.object: at most one pending run, canceling and replacing the existing pending run when a new run is queued
semantic_ast.subject: queue: single

propositions.formalization: DEFINITION: queue = max: |pending(g)| <= 100, in FIFO order; a run queued while pending(g) holds 100 is canceled.

consequences: additional runs are canceled when the queue is full
semantic_ast.object: up to 100 pending runs in a concurrency group and cancel every additional run when the queue is full
semantic_ast.subject: queue: max

entries.expect: is not allowed and will result in a workflow validation error

propositions.formalization: CONSTRAINT: queue = max and cancel-in-progress = true is a workflow validation error.

semantic_ast.subject: the combination of queue: max and cancel-in-progress: true

entries.expect: The concurrency group name is case insensitive

propositions.formalization: DEFINITION: group(a) = group(b) iff casefold(a) = casefold(b).

semantic_ast.object: case insensitive, so prod and Prod name the same group
semantic_ast.subject: the concurrency group name

ambiguities: The docs deny any ordering guarantee while describing FIFO; the model implements strict FIFO as the stated intent and does not claim it is observable.
propositions.formalization: DESCRIPTIVE: pending runs of a group start in order of the time each began waiting; the order is not guaranteed because that time may vary.

semantic_ast.object: jobs or workflow runs in a concurrency group first-in-first-out by the time each started waiting, not the dispatch time
semantic_ast.subject: GitHub Actions

entries.expect: without defining a particular concurrency group
heading_ancestry: Example: Using concurrency to cancel any in-progress job or run

ambiguities: The sentence contradicts the example above it, which sets group to github.ref; preserved without a rule because the group-keyed model cannot represent an absent group that cancels everything.
propositions.formalization: DESCRIPTIVE: the text says a run is canceled with no particular group defined, while the example it describes defines group = ${{ github.ref }}.

semantic_ast.object: any in-progress run of the job or workflow when no particular concurrency group is defined
qualifiers: the example sets group to the ref
semantic_ast.subject: GitHub Actions

ambiguities: The docs do not say whether pull_request_target and the review events define github.head_ref; the model follows the sentence literally.
propositions.formalization: DESCRIPTIVE: github.head_ref is defined only for event = pull_request; elsewhere a group using it without a fallback is a syntax error; the fallback ${{ github.head_ref || github.run_id }} yields the run id.

exceptions: the run ID is unique and defined for every run
semantic_ast.object: defined only on pull_request events, so other events need a fallback such as the run ID to avoid a syntax error
semantic_ast.subject: github.head_ref

entries.expect: concurrency group names must be unique across workflows
heading_ancestry: Example: Only cancel in-progress jobs or runs for the current workflow

ambiguities: The object text states unconditional cancellation of an in-progress job; in-progress cancellation applies only when cancel-in-progress is true.
propositions.formalization: CONSTRAINT: a group is keyed by repository and name, not by workflow; two workflows with one group name share it. A newer run replaces an older pending run in that group; an in-progress run is canceled only when its workflow sets cancel-in-progress: true. Including github.workflow in the group name keeps workflows apart.

semantic_ast.object: unique across workflows in a repository, otherwise any previous in-progress or pending job is canceled regardless of the workflow
semantic_ast.subject: concurrency group names

entries.expect: multiple pushes to a `release/1.2.3` branch would not cancel
heading_ancestry: Example: Only cancel in-progress jobs on specific branches

ambiguities: The example depends on expression evaluation, which the model does not implement; it is preserved without a rule.
propositions.formalization: DESCRIPTIVE: with cancel-in-progress = !contains(github.ref, 'release/'), pushes to a release branch do not cancel in-progress runs; pushes to other branches do.

exceptions: pushes to a release/ branch do not cancel in-progress runs
semantic_ast.object: in-progress runs on non-release branches only
semantic_ast.subject: cancel-in-progress as an expression
